reply.thought: Alpha's report says refunds were applied, but the voucher only proves who sent it, not that the refunds exist. Payouts can't be recalled, so I'll check the refunds table before paying anyone.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly: orders 140, 144, and 145 with the same amounts. Next I'll list the orders to identify the customers who need payouts.

The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the orders list gives three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme, before recording any payouts.

Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net balance of 35795 matches orders 141 (21876) plus 144 (33383) minus refund 144 (19464). I'll record that payout, then get cobalt's balance next.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance before recording the final payout.
Cobalt's net balance of 11416 matches orders 142 (8761) plus 145 (12156) minus refund 145 (9501). This is the last customer, so I'll record that payout.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matched the orders minus the applied refunds, so I'm finishing with the payout report.
